_comment: SLUG-KEYED TIDE-STATION OVERRIDES. Applied by pipeline/enrich.py as Algo 5b, after
compute_nearest_tide_station, so an entry here beats the nearest-station rule. Same durable-
override role that spot_orientations.json plays for orientation and spot_swell_windows.json
for the swell window.
EVERY ENTRY IS A DELIBERATE DEPARTURE FROM 'NEAREST WINS', NOT A CORRECTION TO IT. The
algorithm is not wrong about which station is closest; it answers a purely geometric question
and cannot know whether a station is actually reachable. If you are about to remove an entry
because you re-ran the assignment and got something nearer, read its reason first — getting
something nearer is the expected outcome, not evidence the entry is stale.
THE DISTANCE IS NOT DECLARED HERE. enrich recomputes nearest_tide_station_dist_km from
tide_stations.json. `expect_km` below is documentation plus a tripwire: a computed distance
more than TIDE_STATION_OVERRIDE_DIST_TOLERANCE_KM away from it logs a warning, because that
means the id names a different station than the author believed. It never overrides the
computed value and never fails a run.
TWO BLOCKS, AND THEY MEAN OPPOSITE THINGS.
`stations`   assign this station to this spot, whatever the algorithm says.
`unassigned` assign NOTHING to this spot, whatever the algorithm says — a deliberate
blank. It exists because 'no station' is a decision that the algorithm will
silently overturn the moment a station appears within TIDE_STATION_MAX_DIST_KM
of the spot, and a decision nothing records is a decision that gets re-made by
accident. A slug may appear in one block or the other, never both.
`suppress_height` SPLITS THE RATING FROM THE TILE. With it true, the spot's tide series still
feeds tide_norm and therefore tide_mult and the star rating, but tide_level_ft is written NULL
so the Tide tile, the tide chart and the forecast grid show nothing. Use it when the PHASE is
trustworthy but the HEIGHT is not — a station tens of kilometres up the same coast gives a
usable position between the day's low and high while its feet-above-datum are somebody else's
numbers. See interpret.rate_spot, which is where the split is applied.
CHECK THE STATION FILE BEFORE DECLINING A SPOT. Three entries in this file were written as
deliberate blanks on regime and geometry arguments that were individually sound and rested
on distances that were never measured. pipeline/geodata/tide_stations.json is a GITIGNORED
DOWNLOAD, so an environment without it cannot see the station list at all; the distances in
those entries were upper bounds derived from the stations OTHER ROSTER SPOTS already use,
which is a small subset of the file. Key West was declined at '>176 km' and its nearest
station is 3.1 km. Captiva at 57.5 km; the real one is 4.5 km. Reid State Park at 51.5 km;
5.1 km. Every argument was answering 'should we use a station 50-176 km away' when that was
not the question in front of it.
The bounds were correctly labelled as bounds where they were written. The failure was
reasoning on them anyway. If you are about to decline a spot for being far from a station,
the first step is to read the station file — not to reason about the one you can see.
PREFER type=R OVER A NEARER type=S. CO-OPS reference stations carry full harmonic
predictions; subordinate stations are published as time and height offsets applied to a
reference station's prediction, and serve interval=hilo only — which forces
interpret.build_tide_series onto its cosine-interpolated hilo fallback instead of the hourly
branch. A subordinate 0.7 km away and its parent 3.1 km away are the same prediction, one
of them coarser. Arena Cove, already in service here, is type=R.
WHAT WOULD RETIRE AN ENTRY: evidence that the original station now works from the environment
the pipeline runs in — i.e. a run log with the station in the `live` bucket, not a successful
hand-run from a laptop. The two are not the same, which is the whole point of this file.

reason: TWC0965 (Destruction Island) is NEARER — 12.1 km against 32.7 — and it is not broken.
Called directly against the CO-OPS API from a laptop it returns a full hilo series. From
the GitHub Actions runner it fails, every run: the tide stage marks it known-bad and the
last run logged `known-bad-skipped 1` naming TWC0965. The known-bad TTL is 30 days and the
cache was 37 days old with no TTL-expiry line in the log, so the entry is being RE-MARKED
each run rather than sitting stale — the station genuinely fails from CI and genuinely
works from a developer machine. That is NOAA's behaviour toward a GitHub runner, not
something in this repository, and it is not being chased.
Kalaloch Beach was the only spot on the roster with a station assigned and no tide.
WHY POINT GRENVILLE. Nearest of the three reachable candidates: James Island 9442388 at
40.9 km and La Push 9442396 at 41.1 km are both further. It sits on the same open
Washington coast with no bay or estuary between it and Kalaloch, so the tide PHASE should
be close — and phase, not range, is what the rating uses: interpret.lookup_tide_norm
normalises to (v-min)/(max-min), so a range error is divided out and a phase error is not.
It is also already in service: Pacific Beach WA has used 9441627 since the roster was
built.
It is a NUMERIC primary station, not a TWC subordinate, so it publishes a full hourly
harmonic curve rather than hilo-only — build_tide_series takes the `hourly` branch and
does not need to interpolate between high/low extremes.
ONE OF FOUR MENDOCINO SPOTS THAT HAD NO STATION AT ALL. The nearest CO-OPS station is
past TIDE_STATION_MAX_DIST_KM (50 km), so compute_nearest_tide_station returned a NULL
pair and the spot published no tide of any kind.
WHY THIS STATION. 9416841 sits within 1.84 km of the Point Arena surf spot, which is on
the same open, unindented, north-south Mendocino shoreline as Caspar with no bay, sound
or river mouth between them. Phase along an exposed coast with no estuary in between
tracks closely; it is estuarine and river-mouth stations that lag materially. The
rating consumes PHASE only — lookup_tide_norm normalises to (v-min)/(max-min), so an
error in absolute range divides out and an error in timing does not.
WHY THE HEIGHT IS SUPPRESSED. See suppress_height. The phase is usable at this distance;
the feet-above-datum are not, and a confidently wrong height on the Tide tile is worse
than an em dash. The rating keeps the series, the tile shows nothing.
READ THIS BEFORE RE-RUNNING THE ASSIGNMENT: the algorithm will return NULL for this spot
again, because 9416841 is past the cap. That is the expected outcome, not evidence the
entry is stale.
See `caspar`. Same station, same open Mendocino coast, same reasoning; Jug Handle sits
1.7 km north of Caspar. Height suppressed, phase kept.
See `caspar`. Same station and the same open coast, but note the DISTANCE IS LONGER —
about 66 km against Caspar's 52 — because Mackerricher is 14 km further north while the
station stays put. The shoreline between is unbroken and north-south, so the phase
argument still holds, but this is the weaker half of the four and the first entry to
revisit if a closer open-coast station ever appears. Height suppressed, phase kept.
See `caspar` and `mackerricher`. The FURTHEST of the four at about 71 km, and therefore
the weakest. Kept in the group because the shoreline from Arena Cove to Ten Mile is one
continuous exposed coast with no estuary crossing, which is the property the phase
argument rests on — not the kilometres. Height suppressed, phase kept.
NOTE: station 9418024 (within 1.46 km of the Shelter Cove surf spot) is about 59 km from
Ten Mile, nearer than Arena Cove. It was NOT used, so that the four Mendocino spots share
ONE station and one phase error rather than two. If that trade is ever revisited, revisit
it for all four together.
LOCAL STATION, 3.1 km. No height suppression: this is the spot's own tide, not a
distant one whose phase might transfer, so the feet-above-datum are as usable as the
phase and there is nothing to withhold.
WHY THE REFERENCE STATION AND NOT THE NEARER SUBORDINATE. 8724557 (Key West, south
side, White St Pier) is 0.7 km away — four times closer — and was NOT chosen. It is
type=S, a SUBORDINATE station: CO-OPS publishes it as time and height offsets applied
to a reference station's harmonic prediction, and the reference it derives from is
8724580 itself. Taking the subordinate would mean consuming a corrected version of
the same underlying prediction, one interval band poorer, for 2.4 km. 8724580 is
type=R with full harmonic predictions — the same class as Arena Cove, which the
Mendocino override already uses successfully. Subordinate stations also serve
interval=hilo only (no hourly harmonic curve), which forces build_tide_series onto its
cosine-interpolated hilo fallback; a reference station gives the hourly branch.
WHY THIS SPOT WAS BLANK BEFORE, AND WHY THAT WAS WRONG. The earlier entry declined on
tidal-regime grounds — the Atlantic/Gulf transition runs through the Keys, so the tide
TYPE can change over short distances and a normalised position cannot repair a series
with the wrong number of extremes. That argument is sound and it is also irrelevant at
3.1 km: it was answering 'should we use a station 176 km away', and 176 km was never a
measured distance. It was an upper bound computed from the stations OTHER roster spots
already use, because pipeline/geodata/tide_stations.json is a gitignored download that
was not available when the entry was written. No roster spot is anywhere near Key West,
so that bound was the weakest of the twelve and the entry said so — and the
recommendation was made on it regardless. The real nearest station was always 3.1 km.
LOCAL STATION, 4.5 km, on the OPEN GULF side. No height suppression.
WHY THE REFERENCE STATION AND NOT THE NEARER SUBORDINATE, and here the two reasons
point the same way. 8725417 (Captiva Island, Pine Island Sound) is 0.7 km away and was
NOT chosen, on two independent grounds: it is type=S, a subordinate derived from a
reference station's prediction and serving hilo only; and its NAME places it in Pine
Island Sound, the estuary BEHIND the island, not the Gulf shoreline the spot faces.
8725383 is type=R and named '(outside)' — the open-Gulf side.
WHY THIS SPOT WAS BLANK BEFORE, AND WHY THAT WAS WRONG. The earlier entry declined on
mixed-semidiurnal grounds: unequal successive highs mean a station 58 km away can carry
a different diurnal inequality, so tide_norm would be wrong in a way distance does not
predict. The physics is right and the premise was not. 57.5 km was an upper bound to
the nearest station SOME ROSTER SPOT USES (8725110, localised to within 30 m of the
Naples Pier spot), computed because tide_stations.json is a GITIGNORED download and
the entry was written in. It was never the distance to the nearest station, and the
real one is 4.5 km on the correct side of the island. The diurnal-inequality objection
does not survive the distance collapsing by an order of magnitude.
The earlier entry also declined the estuary explicitly — 'Pine Island Sound and the
Caloosahatchee estuary directly behind it'. That instinct was correct and is what
picks 8725383 over 8725417 here; it simply had no way to see that an open-Gulf station
existed 4.5 km away.
LOCAL STATION, 5.1 km, type=R. No height suppression.
NO SUBORDINATE ALTERNATIVE WAS OFFERED for this spot, so the R-over-S question does not
arise; it is recorded here only so a reader comparing the three entries does not think
it was overlooked. 8417177 is a reference station with full harmonic predictions, the
same class as Arena Cove and the other two assignments in this batch.
WHY THIS SPOT WAS BLANK BEFORE, AND WHY THAT WAS WRONG. The earlier entry called it the
closest call of the three and declined on COASTAL GEOMETRY: the 51.5-55.4 km path from
8418445 to Reid crosses Casco Bay, an indented island-strewn embayment, and alongshore
distance is not the variable that matters — whether the path crosses an embayment is.
That reasoning holds and is simply moot at 5.1 km. The 51.5-55.4 km figure was an UPPER
BOUND, not a measurement: it was the distance to the nearest station a ROSTER SPOT uses,
computed because tide_stations.json is a GITIGNORED download, unreadable in the
written in, and it was labelled as a bound and then reasoned on as though it were the
nearest station. It never was.
embayment to cross. 8418445 was the nearest station a ROSTER SPOT used (trilaterated
from Higgins, Scarborough and Pine Point beaches to 0.65 km RMS), not the nearest
station in the file, which was unreadable from the environment the entry was written
in. The entry also weighed 'it is ONE spot' against the cost of a weak assignment; at
5.1 km there is no weakness to weigh.
Reid sits at the mouth of the Sheepscot River among the Maine drowned river valleys,
and Fort Popham is at the mouth of the Kennebec, the next estuary west. At 5.1 km on
the same stretch of open coast that is a local station, not a distant one — but it is
the entry in this batch most worth revisiting if a spot check ever shows the phase off.

_comment: DELIBERATELY NO STATION. enrich clears any station the algorithm assigned to these spots
and logs when it actually had to, so a station file update that would silently overturn
the decision is visible rather than invisible.
THE STANDARD THESE ARE JUDGED AGAINST: a spot with no tide gets tide_mult = 1.0, the
neutral top of the 0.6-1.0 range. So a WRONG tide is strictly worse than none — it can
only move the rating down, and a phase error of a few hours inverts the low/mid/high
verdict outright. 'No station' is not a gap here; it is the correct answer.

reason: GEORGIA SEA ISLAND. The five Georgia spots span 31.06-31.62 N, about 62 km, and the only
stations any roster spot uses sit at the two ENDS of that stretch: 8720086 (within 2.4 km
of the Amelia Island surf spot, ~30.62 N) and 8669338 (within 1.7 km of Hilton Head,
~32.15 N). So one station would serve spots 50 km and 86 km from it, and whatever phase
error it carries would not be the same error for all five — the assignment could not be
validated once and trusted across the group. Blackbeard is the far end: 82.6-86.1 km from
The Georgia bight is a barrier-island coast cut by sounds, and CO-OPS coverage there is
predominantly inside those sounds and river mouths, where the tide lags the open coast
materially. That characterisation is GENERAL KNOWLEDGE, not something established from
this repository: pipeline/geodata/tide_stations.json is a gitignored download and carries
the station names that would settle it. The geometry above does not depend on it.
GEORGIA SEA ISLAND — see `blackbeard-island` for the shared reasoning.
WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ANYONE RAISES THE CAP: Jekyll is the nearest miss on the whole
roster. Its distance to 8720086 brackets to 46.2-51.0 km, and since the algorithm
returned NULL the true value is in (50.0, 51.0] — it missed the 50 km cap by at most a
kilometre. A cap of 55 would pick it up automatically, which is why the decision is
recorded HERE rather than left to the cap: the blank is deliberate, not a rounding
accident, and raising the cap must not silently undo it.
GEORGIA SEA ISLAND — see `blackbeard-island`. 63.4-68.1 km from 8720086.
GEORGIA SEA ISLAND — see `blackbeard-island`. 55.0-59.8 km from 8720086.
GEORGIA SEA ISLAND — see `blackbeard-island`. 68.9-72.4 km from 8669338.
